action: No action needed; for awareness. UK operators of essential services and their suppliers should track the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill for scope changes.
exec: Pressure is building to widen UK cyber regulation, which could bring more organisations and suppliers into scope.
org: House of Lords National Resilience Committee
plain: A UK parliamentary committee says the government is not taking cyber threats from hostile countries seriously enough and that its new cyber law does not go far enough.
summary: The committee's report says the UK is underprepared for potentially catastrophic risks, including cyberattacks from Russia, China and Iran, and that the Cyber Security and Resilience Bill falls short of the standards needed. It was published eight days before a major Commons vote on the bill. Peers want wider regulatory scope, properly resourced regulators and more openness with the public about threats.
title: House of Lords committee says UK government 'complacent' on hostile-state cyber threats

validation.note: One established outlet reporting the committee's published report; the report itself was not read.

review.note: Compared 16 Nov date, complacent wording, Russia/China/Iran, bill falls short, eight days before vote, regulators and openness against The Record.
